Gene Description

CASP6 (caspase-6, formerly Mch2) is an Asp-directed cysteine endopeptidase synthesized as a short-prodomain zymogen. Proteolytic processing, including context-dependent self-processing, generates the active enzyme. Cytosolic and nuclear CASP6 cleaves substrates including lamins, SATB1, RIPK1 and BID, contributing to apoptotic execution and amplification. In hepatocyte models, CASP3 or CASP7 processing of CASP6 and subsequent BID cleavage sustain a mitochondrial death-signaling loop that is inhibited by AMPK-dependent phosphorylation. Its substrate specificity and activation mechanisms differ from those of CASP3 and CASP7.

Summary: The Human Protein Atlas places CASP6 in the fibrillar center, but the local cache has no image-level evidence and the curated CASP6 literature supports broader cytosolic/nuclear pools.

Core Functions

CASP6 is an Asp-directed cysteine endopeptidase that cleaves protein substrates after VEHD/VEID-like caspase recognition sequences and can activate its own zymogen by intersubunit-linker self-processing at Asp-193/Asp-179.

Molecular Function:
cysteine-type endopeptidase activity
Directly Involved In:
protein autoprocessing
Cellular Locations:
cytosol nucleoplasm
Supporting Evidence:
  • file:human/CASP6/CASP6-uniprot.txt
    Strict requirement for Asp at position P1 and has a preferred cleavage sequence of Val-Glu-His-Asp
  • PMID:7796396
    recombinant Mch2 alpha, but not Mch2 beta, possesses protease activity
  • PMID:19133298
    Casp6 was self-processed and activated in vitro and in vivo
  • PMID:20890311
    intramolecular cleavage at Asp 193 is a prerequisite for CASP6 self-activation

CASP6 carries out apoptotic substrate cleavage in intrinsic and executioner-caspase contexts, including RIPK1 cleavage downstream of cytochrome c/caspase-9 and cleavage of nuclear substrates such as lamins and SATB1.

Molecular Function:
cysteine-type endopeptidase activity
Directly Involved In:
execution phase of apoptosis intrinsic apoptotic signaling pathway
Cellular Locations:
cytosol nucleoplasm
Supporting Evidence:
  • PMID:22858542
    The only apoptotic caspase that cleaved more than 50% of total RIPK1 under these experimental conditions was the executioner caspase-6
  • PMID:18408014
    A SUMO-independent interaction of inactive caspase-6 and SATB1 was noted.
  • Reactome:R-HSA-352268
    Cleaved Satb1 dissociates from chromatin
  • PMID:32029622
    Active caspase-6 cleaved Bid to induce cytochrome c release, generating a feedforward loop that leads to hepatocyte death.
  • PMID:8710882
    Mch2 alpha also cleaved recombinant and nuclear lamin A

Suggested Questions for Experts

Q: Does human CASP6 promote RIPK3–ZBP1 assembly independently of protease activity in native human infection models, as demonstrated with mouse proteins and cells in PMID:32298652?

Suggested experts: Kanneganti TD, Zheng M

Q: Does the Human Protein Atlas fibrillar-center signal reflect endogenous CASP6 localization, apoptotic relocalization, or antibody/background signal, and should this precise HPA component row be retained?

Q: Can the Caco-2 differentiation proteomics study be rechecked for CASP6 perturbation or follow-up evidence, or should the epithelial cell differentiation IEP row be removed as expression-only?

Suggested Experiments

Experiment: Introduce separation-of-function CASP6 truncations and IDR point mutants into CASP6-deficient macrophages and test endogenous RIPK3-ZBP1 co-immunoprecipitation, caspase-1 cleavage, MLKL phosphorylation, and cell death after influenza A virus infection.

Hypothesis: CASP6 bridges RIPK3 to ZBP1 through intrinsically disordered regions independently of its catalytic cysteine.

Type: structure-function rescue assay

Experiment: Perform N-terminomics in isogenic CASP6, CASP3, and CASP7 knockout cells undergoing cytochrome-c/etoposide-driven intrinsic apoptosis and compare endogenous cleavage of RIPK1, BID, lamins, SATB1, vimentin, and MAPT-like substrates.

Hypothesis: CASP6 cleaves a narrow, context-specific substrate set compared with CASP3/CASP7 during intrinsic apoptosis.

Type: degradomics / N-terminomics

CASP6 notes

2026-09-30

  • Re-audited the completed CASP6 review after refreshing GOA and UniProt. GOA
    still has the same 256 source rows and the YAML has no stale or missing rows.
    Tightened the two remaining broad GO:0006915 apoptotic-process assertions
    to GO:0097194 execution phase of apoptosis while keeping separate
    intrinsic-apoptotic-signaling and ZBP1/RIPK3 PANoptosis entries for the
    RIPK1/BID feedback and viral innate-immunity contexts.
  • Completed a manual CASP6 review from cached PubMed records, Reactome events,
    UniProt, GOA, the PTHR10454 PAINT context, and the existing
    Liver apoptosis regulation by CASP6 GO-CAM after provider-backed deep
    research was unavailable.
  • Accepted CASP6's core Asp-directed cysteine endopeptidase activity,
    proteolytic self-activation, broad apoptotic role, RIPK1 cleavage in intrinsic
    apoptosis, and BID/hepatocyte and lamina/SATB1/vimentin substrate contexts as
    valid protease biology.
  • Added a conservative NEW GO:0060090 molecular adaptor activity assertion
    for the protease-independent RIPK3/ZBP1 scaffolding role in influenza
    A-induced PANoptosis, supported by PMID:32298652.
  • Removed 201 of 202 generic GO:0005515 protein binding rows and modified the
    SATB1 row to the informative CASP6 cysteine endopeptidase activity. Most
    removed rows came from the PMID:32814053 systematic yeast two-hybrid
    neurodegeneration interactome or other high-throughput interactome maps.
  • Treated several evidence gaps cautiously: the ATP11C/flippase cleavage row,
    the Caco-2 epithelial differentiation row, the HSP70/GATA1 cytosol row, and
    the Human Protein Atlas fibrillar-center localization row are UNDECIDED
    pending full-text, supplemental, or image-level confirmation.
  • Accepted the valid Reactome cytosol and nucleoplasm localization rows as
    core CASP6 compartment evidence. The remaining mixed-action warnings are
    intentional source-specific exceptions: an abstract-only ATP11C row, an
    abstract-only HSP70/GATA1 cytosol row, a TP53 expression event that projects
    CASP6 as product rather than actor, and a CAFA row from a DFF40/CAD paper
    without CASP6-specific evidence.
  • Marked the HIP14 palmitoylation row as MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED for CASP6
    because CASP6 is the inhibited target in that experiment, removed the TP53
    expression Reactome cytosol projection, and removed the CAFA staurosporine
    row from the DFF40/CAD paper because the cached full text contains no
    CASP6-specific evidence.

2026-10-25 comparative apoptotic-execution review

Systematically examined all 257 rows, preserving every imported annotation payload. Decisions judge the biological claim, not the evidence code: independently established cysteine endopeptidase activity, cytosolic/nuclear localization and apoptotic execution are retained/refined even when one original citation is not sufficient alone. No experimental claim is rejected merely because the cached abstract foregrounds a different protein. Bare protein-binding removals mean uninformative annotation, not false interaction.

Species and paralogs: human CASP3/CASP7 have distinct natural-substrate profiles (PMID:18723680). Mouse CASP7 can cleave ICAD efficiently and contributes to strain-dependent compensation for Casp3 loss (PMID:15525783). The 129X1/SvJ versus C57BL/6J comparison in PMID:12152782 must not be conflated with the 129S1/SvImJ comparison in PMID:15525783. These results do not establish universal redundancy or a single obligatory executioner across tissues.

CASP6: full PMID:32029622 establishes direct CASP3/CASP7 cleavage of procaspase-6 in vitro, HepG2 processing and a CASP6–BID mitochondrial feedback mechanism. It does not justify a universal initiator-caspase activation route. Full PMID:32298652 and public primary Figure 6A identify mouse CASP6/RIPK3 constructs despite the HEK293T host; native infection experiments also use mouse cells/mice. Human prior NEW adaptor annotation is retired/UNDECIDED; conserved contextual human immune claims remain explicitly comparative. Mouse IAV findings do not imply a requirement for all inflammasome triggers.

CASP7: full PMID:35705808 establishes mouse SMPD1 processing and membrane-pore repair. CASP7 performs proteolytic maturation; SMPD1 performs ceramide-producing lipid hydrolysis. Repair delays lysis in the tested settings, so this mechanism is not universally pro-lytic. PMID:22464733 distinguishes PARP1 cleavage from PARP1 poly-ADP-ribosylation activity.

Evidence handling: checked existing primary caches and retained unresolved precise cellular/stimulus claims as UNDECIDED where evidence could not establish the claim. 0 pre-existing nonverbatim deep-research quotations were removed from the optional quotation field; source citations and review rationales remain, with direct primary evidence preferred for core functions. Provider reports remain immutable. Existing reports were used where present; missing Falcon reports were attempted with perplexity-lite fallback, and failures are recorded in .cache/module-audit-logs/apoptosis-caspase-*-research.log. No missing report was fabricated. Sources were fetched through normal helpers only.

Verified UniProt PANTHER placement: PTHR10454 CASPASE; CASP3/Casp3 SF198 CASPASE-3, CASP6/Casp6 SF206 CASPASE-6, CASP7/Casp7 SF31 CASPASE-7. These are membership checks, not assertions of identical physiological deployment.

The annotation-reviewer consultation confirmed that true same-target catalytic/location claims should not be removed for citation weakness, and that substrate cleavage is not the same as the substrate's enzymatic reaction. Notes are comparative; only target-specific claims are asserted in the review.

PMID:8710882 normal fetch succeeded on retry (abstract only; PMC XML/HTML/PDF unavailable through helper). Explicit recombinant human CASP6-versus-CASP3 comparison supports lamin-A specificity. PMID:8663580 separately reports granzyme-B-mediated Mch2 processing. Neither supports a universal initiator-caspase activation route.

  review:
    summary: CASP6 has independently established cysteine-type endopeptidase activity.
    action: ACCEPT
    reason: CASP6 has independently established cysteine-type endopeptidase activity. The catalytic cysteine
      and Asp-directed substrate cleavage distinguish caspases from aspartic proteases. A source that does not
      isolate this activity by itself does not negate the same-target biochemical claim; the original citation
      remains preserved for provenance.
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: file:human/CASP6/CASP6-uniprot.txt
      record_section: ["CC:SIMILARITY"]
      supporting_text: Belongs to the peptidase C14A family.
    - reference_id: PMID:32029622
      supporting_text: active caspase-6 cleaved purified Bcl2 family protein Bid

  - UniProtKB:Q01826
  review:
    summary: The SATB1 interaction is a substrate/enzyme context for CASP6 cleavage, not an informative
      standalone binding activity.
    action: MODIFY
    reason: SATB1 is a nuclear substrate whose caspase cleavage is enhanced by sumoylation; the useful CASP6
      molecular-function assertion is cysteine-type endopeptidase activity rather than generic protein
      binding.
    proposed_replacement_terms:
    - id: GO:0004197
      label: cysteine-type endopeptidase activity
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:18408014
      supporting_text: A SUMO-independent interaction of inactive caspase-6 and SATB1 was noted.
      reference_section_type: ABSTRACT
    - reference_id: Reactome:R-HSA-352268
      supporting_text: Cleaved Satb1 dissociates from chromatin

    id: GO:0005829
    label: cytosol
  evidence_type: IDA
  original_reference_id: GO_REF:0000052
  qualifier: located_in
  review:
    summary: CASP6 has a cytosolic pool that participates in apoptotic and innate-immune signaling.
    action: ACCEPT
    reason: Cytosolic CASP6 is consistent with its intrinsic-apoptosis RIPK1 cleavage and its ZBP1/RIPK3 role;
      the Reactome vimentin and translocation events are valid but only localization support.
    supported_by:

      signaling when AMPK inhibition is relieved.

    relevance: HIGH

    review_notes: 'Full text inspected: native mouse liver perturbation, HepG2 experiments and purified cleavage
      assays support a context-dependent CASP3/7–CASP6–BID feedforward mechanism. Peptide substrates/inhibitors
      are not entirely caspase-specific; genetic depletion corroborates the role.'

core_functions:
- description: CASP6 is an Asp-directed cysteine endopeptidase that cleaves protein substrates after
    VEHD/VEID-like caspase recognition sequences and can activate its own zymogen by intersubunit-linker
    self-processing at Asp-193/Asp-179.
  molecular_function:
    id: GO:0004197
    label: cysteine-type endopeptidase activity
  directly_involved_in:
  - id: GO:0016540
    label: protein autoprocessing
  locations:
  - id: GO:0005829
    label: cytosol
  - id: GO:0005654
    label: nucleoplasm
  supported_by:
  - reference_id: file:human/CASP6/CASP6-uniprot.txt
    record_section: ["CC:CATALYTIC ACTIVITY"]
    supporting_text: "Strict requirement for Asp at position P1 and has a preferred\n        cleavage sequence of
      Val-Glu-His-Asp"
  - reference_id: PMID:7796396
    supporting_text: 'recombinant Mch2 alpha, but

      not Mch2 beta, possesses protease activity'
    reference_section_type: ABSTRACT
  - reference_id: PMID:19133298
    supporting_text: Casp6 was self-processed and activated in vitro and in vivo
    reference_section_type: ABSTRACT
  - reference_id: PMID:20890311
    supporting_text: intramolecular cleavage at Asp 193 is a prerequisite for CASP6 self-activation
    reference_section_type: ABSTRACT
- description: CASP6 carries out apoptotic substrate cleavage in intrinsic and executioner-caspase contexts,
    including RIPK1 cleavage downstream of cytochrome c/caspase-9 and cleavage of nuclear substrates such as
    lamins and SATB1.
  molecular_function:
    id: GO:0004197
    label: cysteine-type endopeptidase activity
  directly_involved_in:
  - id: GO:0097194
    label: execution phase of apoptosis
  - id: GO:0097193
    label: intrinsic apoptotic signaling pathway
  locations:
  - id: GO:0005829
    label: cytosol
  - id: GO:0005654
    label: nucleoplasm
  supported_by:
  - reference_id: PMID:22858542
    supporting_text: The only apoptotic caspase that cleaved more than 50% of total RIPK1 under these
      experimental conditions was the executioner caspase-6
  - reference_id: PMID:18408014
    supporting_text: A SUMO-independent interaction of inactive caspase-6 and SATB1 was noted.
    reference_section_type: ABSTRACT
  - reference_id: Reactome:R-HSA-352268
    supporting_text: Cleaved Satb1 dissociates from chromatin
  - reference_id: PMID:32029622
    supporting_text: 'Active caspase-6 cleaved Bid to induce cytochrome c release, generating a

      feedforward loop that leads to hepatocyte death.'
    reference_section_type: ABSTRACT
  - reference_id: PMID:8710882
    supporting_text: Mch2 alpha also cleaved recombinant and nuclear lamin A
proposed_new_terms: []
suggested_questions:
- question: Does human CASP6 promote RIPK3–ZBP1 assembly independently of protease activity in native human
    infection models, as demonstrated with mouse proteins and cells in PMID:32298652?
  experts:
  - Kanneganti TD
  - Zheng M
- question: Does the Human Protein Atlas fibrillar-center signal reflect endogenous CASP6 localization,
    apoptotic relocalization, or antibody/background signal, and should this precise HPA component row be
    retained?
  experts: []
- question: Can the Caco-2 differentiation proteomics study be rechecked for CASP6 perturbation or follow-up
    evidence, or should the epithelial cell differentiation IEP row be removed as expression-only?
  experts: []
suggested_experiments:
- hypothesis: CASP6 bridges RIPK3 to ZBP1 through intrinsically disordered regions independently of its
    catalytic cysteine.
  description: Introduce separation-of-function CASP6 truncations and IDR point mutants into CASP6-deficient
    macrophages and test endogenous RIPK3-ZBP1 co-immunoprecipitation, caspase-1 cleavage, MLKL
    phosphorylation, and cell death after influenza A virus infection.
  experiment_type: structure-function rescue assay
- hypothesis: CASP6 cleaves a narrow, context-specific substrate set compared with CASP3/CASP7 during
    intrinsic apoptosis.
  description: Perform N-terminomics in isogenic CASP6, CASP3, and CASP7 knockout cells undergoing
    cytochrome-c/etoposide-driven intrinsic apoptosis and compare endogenous cleavage of RIPK1, BID, lamins,
    SATB1, vimentin, and MAPT-like substrates.
  experiment_type: degradomics / N-terminomics
